customer-alex: Hey team — noticed a spike in 429s and a lot of perceived throttling after we turned on prefetch/kv and bumped continuous batching. It only shows up under short bursts (burst ~150-250 RPS). Any quick checks? :confused:

maria-support: Sorry you're seeing that. Can you share a minimal repro request (curl) and the X-RateLimit* headers from a failing response? Also the model and typical sequence length helps.

customer-alex: Model: open-30b (hosted), seq ~400 tokens typical. We enabled kv_prefetch=true and continuous_batching=enabled, max_batch_size=64. Example failing curl:```bash
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-30b","input":"hello","max_tokens":400}' &
done; wait
```
When it fails the body is `{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}` and the headers include `x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 600` and `x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0` sometimes.

thomas-sre: Thanks — a few likely interactions: continuous batching increases pooling and can cause more tokens queued per request which raises token consumption per second, kv prefetch increases cache traffic and may cause short-lived token spikes when cache misses trigger full decoding. Together those can exhaust burst quota windows.

maria-support: Can you also paste a raw failing response headers block? We want to confirm which bucket (token vs request) is tripping. If `x-rw-ratelimit-reset` is small (few secs) it's burst; if long it's quota exhaustion.

customer-alex: here's a sample header dump from a failing call:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 600
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 7
x-rw-quota-tokens: 12000
x-rw-quota-remaining: 50
```

eng-runtime-liz: That looks like the per-minute/burst bucket is hitting zero (`remaining: 0` and reset 7s). Two suggestions to triage quickly: 1) disable kv_prefetch temporarily to see if cache miss storms are contributing; 2) reduce `max_batch_size` to 16 or 8 and/or lower concurrent clients so token spike per-second drops.

thomas-sre: For repro steps we recommend a deterministic load test: run a k6 script that does a controlled ramp with fixed concurrency and fixed seq len (400) and capture `x-rw-ratelimit-*` headers across time. If you can reproduce, attach the raw k6 logs and we can correlate with infra metrics (burst_capacity, batch_size distribution, kv miss rate).

maria-support: Quick workaround in-prod: set `continuous_batching=false` on the route or set `max_batch_size` to a lower value and enable `local_kv_cache=false` until we confirm behavior. That sacrifices some cost efficiency but reduces sudden token bursts.

customer-alex: OK will try toggling kv_prefetch off and lower batch size. One question — is there a way to increase burst window or reserve capacity for a customer to avoid these short 429 storms?

eng-runtime-liz: Yes — we can provision a small dedicated burst pool / reserved burst capacity for your org or bump route-level burst_limit. For an immediate band-aid we can also raise the per-minute token quota for your account while we investigate. I'll open an infra ticket if you want us to do that.

maria-support: Please send the k6 output + a trace_id from a failing request (x-rw-trace-id header) and we’ll escalate. If you want, we can schedule a quick run with us watching dashboards and toggling config live. :+1:

opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-8743 — "customer-alex perceived throttling after kv prefetch + continuous batching". Assigned to eng-runtime-liz and thomas-sre.

customer-alex: Thanks — will attach logs in the ticket and try the suggested toggles. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:
